entries.content_plain:
CHAPTER 24
 
Ex 24:1-18. Delivery of the Law and Covenant.

3-4. Moses came and told the people all the words of the Lord--The rehearsal of the foregoing laws and the ten commandments, together with the promises of special blessings in the event of their obedience, having drawn forth from the people a unanimous declaration of their consent, it was forthwith recorded as the conditions of the national covenant. The next day preparations were made for having it (the covenant) solemnly ratified, by building an altar and twelve pillars; the altar representing God, and the pillars the tribes of Israel--the two parties in this solemn compact--while Moses acted as typical mediator.
entries.reader_content_plain: 3-4. The next day preparations were made for having it (the covenant) solemnly ratified, by building an altar and twelve pillars; the altar representing God, and the pillars the tribes of Israel--the two parties in this solemn compact--while Moses acted as typical mediator.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv822"/><div sID="gen1146" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv822"/><hi type="bold">8. Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people--</hi>probably on the twelve pillars, as representing the people (also the book, <reference osisRef="Heb.9.19">He 9:19</reference>), and the act was accompanied by a public proclamation of its import. It was setting their seal to the covenant (compare <reference osisRef="1Cor.11.25">1Co 11:25</reference>). It must have been a deeply impressive, as well as instructive scene, for it taught the Israelites that the covenant was made with them only through the sprinkling of blood--that the divine acceptance of themselves and services, was only by virtue of an atoning sacrifice, and that even the blessings of the national covenant were promised and secured to them only through grace. The ceremonial, however, had a further and higher significance, as is shown by the apostle (see as above). <div eID="gen1146" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv824"/><div sID="gen1150" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv824"/><hi type="bold">10. And they saw the God of Israel--</hi>That there was no visible form or representation of the divine nature, we have expressly intimated (<reference osisRef="Deut.4.15">De 4:15</reference>). But a symbol or emblem of His glory was distinctly, and at a distance, displayed before those chosen witnesses. Many think, however, that in this private scene was discovered, amid the luminous blaze, the faint adumbrated form of the humanity of Christ (<reference osisRef="Ezek.1.26">Eze 1:26</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Gal.3.24">Ga 3:24</reference>).<div eID="gen1150" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1151" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">sapphire--</hi>one of the most valuable and lustrous of the precious gems--of a sky-blue or light azure color and frequently chosen to describe the throne of God (see <reference osisRef="Ezek.1.26">Eze 1:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="1Cor.10.1">10:1</reference>). <div eID="gen1151" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain:
10. And they saw the God of Israel--That there was no visible form or representation of the divine nature, we have expressly intimated (De 4:15). But a symbol or emblem of His glory was distinctly, and at a distance, displayed before those chosen witnesses. Many think, however, that in this private scene was discovered, amid the luminous blaze, the faint adumbrated form of the humanity of Christ (Eze 1:26; compare Ga 3:24).

18. Moses went into the midst of the cloud--the visible token of God's presence. Divine grace animated and supported him to enter with holy boldness.
 
Moses was in the mount forty days and forty nights--The six days spent in waiting are not included. During that protracted period he was miraculously supported (De 9:9), on a peak scarcely thirty paces in compass.
